log: Working out who would actually buy this
Discovering candidates and exact source URLs (stage 1 of 2)
Fetching up to 10 exact URLs; validating against at most 48,000 characters
Evaluating candidates against 10 fetched pages (stage 2 of 2)

Coverage gaps and failed searches: Reddit returned almost nothing usable — site:reddit.com queries were rewritten by the engine and surfaced vendor and affiliate pages instead of threads, so first-person agency and founder voices are thinner than they should be. Search results for this category are heavily polluted by SEO affiliate comparison content and by Plausible's own pages, which were discounted as buyer evidence. I could not retrieve the one negative WordPress review (wordpress.org/support/topic/requires-registration-and-payment/ returned 404 on fetch; it appears in search results only), and the reviews index page fetch showed only titles, so negative-review wording is unverified. Nothing was found quantifying the public sector population, procurement volumes, or whether the Scottish/Welsh deployments are paid cloud or self-hosted — that distinction matters and is unresolved. No independent evidence was found for e-commerce/Shopify merchants or for EU SMBs buying through web hosts, so neither was proposed. Healthcare evidence covers the trigger only, never a purchase. Population counts are unknown throughout, and fit is left at zero as instructed; the white-label/Sites API capabilities central to the platform candidate are absent from the supplied capability catalogue and so are flagged as unknown rather than supported.
7 audience(s) mapped; 0 worth exploring first. Commercial priority is a hypothesis, not a response-rate forecast.
